adventure.title: The Glass Saint
adventure.synopsis: A museum reliquary bursts on the eve of Saint Olyra’s procession. Before sunset, independent witnesses must recover its stolen petition-bed, expose the lie beneath the city’s obedient saint, and decide whether grief may borrow a body and command through every bell.
adventure.premise: At noon on the eve of Saint Olyra’s procession, the rehearsal bell bursts the museum reliquary from within. The painted devotional copy remains; the engraved silver bed beneath it has been cut away. Curator Iria Vale invokes the emergency witness charter, opening the sealed gallery, restricted archive, procession court, and abandoned bell chapel to independent inspection. Her authority ends at Vale Manor, where her family keeps Olyra’s true heartglass, and her interest prevents her from certifying the case against them. The council will not halt the sunset procession without proof of immediate danger. Witnesses, records, petitioners, bellkeepers, and the divided Vales can establish what Tavia Sorn stole, what Olyra died doing, and what Edrin Vale has built to make the city hear. A warrant, a public case, a broken peal, a bargain, or forced entry may reach the winter garden. None decides who should hold the relic or what the recovered truth requires.
adventure.explanation:
Sixty-three years ago, museum founder and former council archivist Alis Vale replaced Saint Olyra’s heartglass with a painted devotional copy. During the Ash Fever, Olyra defied the council, opened the sealed west infirmary, and died among the patients she refused to abandon. The civic cult kept her authority by reversing her act: Olyra became the saint of obedience. Alis hid her deposition and the names of the patrons who ordered the doors sealed, but kept the authentic heartglass at Vale Manor. The trustees found the substitution during recent conservation and chose silence again.

Alis’s grandson Edrin has spent years authenticating the record. When the trustees offered one more closed review after the procession, he chose the hour when the city would already be listening. Assistant conservator Tavia Sorn joined him because the withheld material included her family’s petitions and an ancestor’s infirmary record. She set a bell-metal answer-pin beneath the case. The rehearsal note made it ring, threw the glass outward, and hid her removal of the silver vow-bed. Tavia carried the bed through the procession court, passed it to Edrin, and fled with a cut archive leaf toward the House of Petitions. She expects the rite to give the buried record a voice. She does not know that it takes one.

The rite joins four materials: Olyra’s heartglass, the petition-engraved vow-bed, knot geometry rehearsed in the Bell Chapel, and panes from Olyra’s first shrine. Six decades of pleas, thanks, slogans, and demands give the silver its language. The heartglass contributes a residue of Olyra, never a recoverable person. The procession peal gives the result reach. The first long note raises a body from reflected petitions. The second takes the natural voice of the nearest living Vale inside the winter garden’s outer pane circle. The third sends one command through every fitted procession bell until dawn. Edrin begins on the speaker mark and intends to pay the vocal cost. Iria is endangered only if she enters the circle or remains there after Edrin is moved beyond it. The mouth stage fails without either a Vale inside or a hand closing the inner line.

Six answer-pins cast from the old infirmary bell connect the apparatus. The museum trigger is cracked and spent. Three pins in the Grand Belfry carry the witness, mouth, and crown notes. Relay pins at East Gate and River Ward repeat the crown command but cannot raise the body or take a speaker. The chapel holds a working counterkey: a notched tuning strip that identifies and lifts live pins, a braided reversal cord that changes the outer knot, and a pitch table keyed to Olyra’s deposition. Each part enables different work. At the belfry, investigators can prevent a stage, confine the crown note, sound a warning, or preserve the peal; every cut rope, lifted pin, and altered knot remains altered.

The investigation contests who may make a fact public. Provost Helian Dorr and the trustees fear riot, scandal, and institutional ruin. They will preserve the procession until confronted with evidence they cannot fold back into a private review. The House of Petitions claims the vow-bed as public property and can provide witnesses, custodians, or current petitions. Bellmaster Jori Kest can delay, mute, or retune the peal when given technical proof and either lawful or public protection. Edrin will pause for a hearing that already possesses records, witnesses, and a custody plan. He will not surrender to another sealed promise. The finale may preserve or destroy the heartglass, dismantle the speaking body, permit a bounded answering rite, or allow the full awakening. Whatever speaks is a composite of relic, record, petition, and civic expectation: a disputed civic voice assembled by the living.

Advance pressure through acts the table can see. Dorr issues containment after a report, accusation, or request reaches him. The answer-pins wake after Edrin has assembled the manor apparatus and Dorr has authorized the final bell test. The procession moves when its hold expires or fails. The first note needs the grand-tower crew; the second needs Edrin to close the inner knot around a Vale; the third needs the crown bell and an intact launch pin. Change any of those facts and the sequence changes. Edrin and Dorr learn through runners, watch reports, public bells, and witnesses. Neither answers information that never reaches him.

Carry five public facts from scene to scene: how widely the rupture’s cause is known; where authenticated copies are held; what authority Captain Renn possesses; whether the procession follows its published course; and which witnesses have committed to speak. These facts persist. A public copy cannot be recalled, a signed witness keeps the commitment, and a written denial becomes evidence of its own. Gains may conflict: publicity can protect records and frighten families; a warrant can secure objects and concentrate them under one seal. Carry those mixed results into the belfry and manor.

Keep four pages distinct during route-open play. **Access** names the doors, routes, and scheduled spaces that can be reached. **Knowledge** names supported claims. **Authority** names what a charter, seal, warrant, custodian, or witness permits. **Ritual state** names the pins, knots, materials, notes, and relays still in play. Knowledge of a place grants no entry; a warrant proves no history; a maintenance passage supplies no counterkey; a stopped bell settles no custody. When separated investigators reunite, record what each saw, changed, received permission for, or still only infers.

Unvisited places continue through fixed hands and channels. Tavia goes from the court to the House unless intercepted. Dorr acts on reports that reach him. Senna logs and protects the archive; publication requires someone present to choose and carry a packet. Petition caucuses carry their own copies and demands. The chapel counterkey stays where Edrin left it until someone removes it. The belfry crew follows the latest order and evidence placed before them. Record each off-screen movement. Late arrival changes custody, access, and pressure; the location and its people retain what has already happened.

Before the winter-garden doors open, carry forward the facts already made. Record the surviving stage and relay pins, any warning peal, the holders of the records, Renn’s authority, the witnesses in motion, and the positions of Iria and Tavia. Six ways into the winter garden remain: a warranted carriage gate, Iria’s family claim, Tavia’s service route, the infirmary-frame maintenance passage, a public advance behind the warning crowd, or direct force. Each brings different witnesses, hazards, and claims to custody.

The winter garden binds five things the rite cannot lose: the shrine-pane crown, the vow-bed, the heartglass cradle, the inner mouth knot, and the bell trunk under the floor. The mouth note takes the nearest living Vale inside the outer pane circle when the note completes. Edrin begins nearest. Iria becomes the target only by entering or remaining inside after he leaves. The ordinary transfer fails without a Vale inside the circle or a hand closing the inner line. The complete counterkey can instead bind a willing breath-giver into a limited answering form. That speaker risks muteness until dawn rather than involuntary permanent loss.

First decide what the bells did to a body and voice. Then decide what the city does with it. Record whether the body formed, whose voice was taken, the command and its range, the surviving condition and custodian of every object, the witnesses to each stage, and all injuries or detentions. Then record publication, prosecution, surviving compulsion, and Olyra’s changed public memory. Edrin’s surrender and silent bells leave the public argument intact. The city may recover the truth of Olyra’s defiance and still disagree about ownership, punishment, sainthood, and what defiance demands now.

encounters.title: The Shattered Gallery
encounters.summary: The broken case yields three evidence chains while museum, watch, and trustee authority compete to seal them first.
encounters.opening_view: One last sliver drops from the saint’s case and rings against the floor. Lio Marr bleeds beside the plinth while Ossa Pell chalks the curved spray. The painted figure still hangs in place; beneath it, a clean silver-bed rectangle remains. Provost Dorr calls for the procession doors. Iria Vale spreads the witness charter across his seal before anyone can close the room.
encounters.content:
The rehearsal leaves docent Lio Marr bleeding, a crowd against the doors, and three offices reaching for the wreckage. Iria Vale lays down the emergency witness charter. It permits independent inspection of museum rooms, consensual staff interviews, counter-signed copies, and a written entry whenever evidence moves. It grants no search of private Vale property, compelled testimony, or ownership. Captain Ors Renn can seal the gallery and detain a named suspect. Floor warden Ossa Pell controls keys and handling. Provost Helian Dorr, procession marshal and senior trustee, wants a vandalism report and open doors before sunset. Registrar Senna Drail has taken the archive keys below. Tavia Sorn is absent from roll call.

The painted bone copy remains strapped to cracked plaster. The clean rectangle beneath it held the engraved silver vow-bed. A hidden answer-pin caught the rehearsal note and threw the case glass outward. One mounting screw was loosened in advance; the second was cut during the panic. Packing felt bears Vale carriage wax. Tavia’s numbered narrow saw is gone. Lio saw a grey museum cloak pass through the service door while the room watched the glass. Ossa can trace every key, though she saw no hand lift the silver.

Sort the scene into three evidence chains. The answer-pin and bell dust establish mechanism. The saw, cut mounts, and cloak route establish removal. The felt, wax, and accession number establish provenance and destination. Leave a chain under watch seals, bag it through Ossa with counter-signatures, or take a sample and exact rubbing while the original stays. Watch custody best supports a warrant. Senna’s certification best supports authenticity. Distributed rubbings and statements survive suppression but invite Dorr to call them incomplete. If he gains the originals, preserve what has already left the room: Lio’s statement, investigators’ notes, and every signed copy. The next problem becomes access, not forgotten discovery.

Several jobs can proceed at once. Treat Lio and gain a calm witness. Reconstruct the service-door sight line before boots destroy it. Give Renn a usable description of the stolen silver. Keep Dorr from reopening the gallery before Ossa closes the log. A poor search still finds the outward spray and exact absence. A lost argument produces Dorr’s written order and the objects he chose to seal. Rough handling contaminates one chain, not the whole case. The evidence points toward the court witnesses, the accession record, the chapel’s pin work, the west infirmary named on the backing, and the Vale carriage route. A rush to the manor remains possible; it arrives with less law and fewer witnesses.

**If skipped or left early.** Ossa numbers the evidence, Renn seals the room, and Dorr places unclaimed originals under trustee seal. Lio receives treatment and remains available. The outward rupture, silver-shaped absence, and staff roll stay observable. Tavia reaches the Procession Court, and every copy or note already made continues to circulate. Later entry may require Senna, Renn, or a written challenge to Dorr. The gallery never resets.

encounters.title: The Procession Court
encounters.summary: A collapsing civic rehearsal turns Tavia’s transfer into partial public testimony and forces an early choice between pursuit, protection, and publication.
encounters.opening_view: “Stop opening empty carts,” Sergeant Vela Rusk shouts. The petition wagon has sagged under a weight it no longer carries, and a grey museum cloak is trapped beneath its wheel. Lantern children are already being formed into ranks. A copyist runs with a loose page; a trustee’s deputy follows. At the far gate, the Vale carriage turns once in the sun and disappears into traffic.
encounters.content:
The procession’s fixed order makes every break visible. Six watch outriders clear the route. Twenty-four children carry glass lanterns under schoolmistress Anet Vey. Four museum porters bear the silver canopy. A petition wagon and three House copyists follow. West Door families carry white ribbons for the Ash Fever dead; Dorr and the civic officers close the line. The devotional image used outdoors is separate from the shattered case, so Dorr can truthfully say the ceremony can proceed. Sergeant Vela Rusk’s detail is searching carts without knowing what the stolen silver looks like.

Tavia crossed the court in a grey museum cloak with the vow-bed under the petition wagon. Lantern bearer Pellen Vey saw the slats bow. Driver Hara Bex felt the weight and later found fresh Vale wax on a replacement strap. Copyists Iven Quill and Sera Mott saw Edrin’s carriage pause and heard Tavia say, “The city gets the words before you get the bell.” When Officer Den Rusk stopped the wagon, she abandoned the cloak, passed the wrapped silver into the carriage, kept a packet of copied records, and fled toward the House of Petitions. Each witness owns one piece. Assemble the handoff; no statement supplies it whole.

Choose what the court preserves. Pursuit may catch or shadow Tavia before the House. Counter-signed statements give Renn the Vale destination and protect witnesses from later claims of crowd invention. A precise description of the vow-bed releases innocent carts and turns panic into a theft search. Crowd control keeps children, wheels, and glass lanterns from becoming injuries. Public accusation makes suppression harder. The West Door families may remain in the line, withdraw, or carry their ribbons with the evidence; the ceremony changes around that choice.

Public pressure follows acts. Name the silver and carriage before witnesses, and rumor becomes an allegation with owners. Put authenticated pages into the crowd, and Dorr loses the comfort of “vandalism.” Win petitioner or West Door commitments, and the accusation acquires a body. Each gain has a cost: Dorr may advance the procession, trustees may order seizure, and frightened families may leave. Quiet protection can preserve a witness who matters more at the manor than a shouted claim does here.

Tavia’s route fails forward. Intercepted, she admits cutting the bed free, refuses trustee return, and asks for a public custodian; she knows nothing of the vocal cost. Shadowed, she reveals the House’s entrances and allies. Lost, she distributes the cut archive leaf and becomes harder to detain privately. Violence lets her escape, but Pellen, Hara, and at least one copyist remain. Meanwhile the procession continues to take position. Delay changes people, orders, and routes rather than subtracting invisible minutes.

**If skipped or reached late.** Tavia reaches the House with the cut leaf. Edrin’s carriage continues to the manor. The procession advances. Pellen stays with the lantern children, Hara returns to the wagon yard, Iven and Sera go to the House, and Den reports to Renn. Their partial accounts remain available. A late investigation follows people and changed ranks, not a preserved chase.

encounters.title: The Archive Vault
encounters.summary: Four record packets prove substitution, suppressed history, modern concealment, and ritual contact—but custody determines what each proof can do.
encounters.opening_view: Three books lie open to the same accession. Heartglass. Substitute. Missing leaf. Registrar Senna Drail checks the pale torn edge of the newest gap, then covers an unsigned deposition with one hand. The vault door stands open only as far as its chain permits. Beside her keys, the custody log waits for its first name.
encounters.content:
Registrar Senna Drail has chained the vault door with junior copyists Eren Sol and Mave Kitt inside. She honors Iria’s charter, provided every drawer, broken seal, and produced copy enters the custody log. Dorr can suspend museum access; he cannot unmake a witnessed page. Senna will certify exact copies for a lawful recipient or investigators prepared to defend her office. She will not smuggle originals. The conservation stair offers faster covert entry, but sacrifices her public signature and may cost her position.

Four packets compete for the copyists’ hands. The **relic packet** joins accession numbers, conservation photographs, donor letters, and a private receipt proving Alis substituted the painted copy and kept the heartglass at Vale Manor. The **Olyra packet** joins her unsigned deposition, council wax, patient indexes, and sermons that turn refusal into obedience. The **modern suppression packet** contains the six-week-old conservation finding and the trustee minute calling it “credible and materially significant” while postponing publication. The **ritual-contact packet** holds Tavia’s slips, Edrin’s consultation requests, Alis’s warning that a Vale voice may become common property, and the chapel-to-garden bell diagram.

Each packet opens different action. Relic records plus the gallery trail support recovery of the vow-bed. Modern suppression plus an independent witness exposes Dorr’s present obstruction. Olyra’s papers plus the infirmary’s material record authenticate the history. Ritual contact plus an answer-pin supports emergency inspection at the belfry or manor. One certified packet can leave quickly. Two require divided labor and two custodians. A complete set before sunset demands an open vault, outside copyists, or rough copies Dorr can challenge.

Custody gives evidence its reach. A watch seal carries immediate legal force but may lock the packet inside a trustee dispute. Senna’s seal carries museum authentication and endangers her office. The House makes copies public and vulnerable to charges of partisanship. The infirmary lends independent history; Caldra will not turn a working hospice into the city’s warehouse. Distributed copies survive seizure only if signatures preserve their chain. Often the strongest case places different packets in different hands.

If Dorr takes the vault, he seals drawers, removes Senna from duty, and sends one copy to the Trustees’ Chamber. That act creates delay and a named obstruction. It leaves family copies, accession gaps, Tavia’s cut leaf, and every certified packet untouched. Stolen papers retain information but acquire a custody objection. When Senna refuses a dangerous request, she names the evidence or recipient that would let her sign. Reward a chosen packet and a defended custodian; the vault cannot yield everything before sunset.

**If skipped or reached late.** Senna protects the originals and logs every order. She chooses no packet for absent investigators. A suspension closes the public stair and enters Dorr’s signature in the book; the conservation stair, a lawful recipient, or divided trustees can reopen access. Tavia’s cut leaf proves one suppressed passage, never the full relic, Olyra, suppression, or ritual chain. Delay narrows authentication without deleting the archive.

encounters.title: The Trustees’ Chamber
encounters.summary: A divided hearing converts distinct kinds of proof into warrants, delay, public record, or a signed refusal that can travel farther.
encounters.opening_view: Each burst of applause from the court shortens the trustees’ silence. Iria Vale’s empty chair faces the museum seal. Beside Provost Dorr, a clerk has begun two incompatible orders: hold the crown bell for a quarter hour; seize the House of Petitions’ ledgers. Witnesses are called in the order Dorr chooses. The ink remains wet enough for either order to become the city’s answer.
encounters.content:
Four trustees have different breaking points. Helian Dorr controls the agenda and procession seal; he trades minutes for order and resists publication he cannot stage-manage. Collections keeper Irena Moss accepts split custody and a manor recovery warrant when the relic is endangered, but keeps originals away from crowds. Halwen Gorse speaks for guilds and merchants; danger to spectators buys a short delay. Maelin Tress speaks for the west wards and breaks with Dorr once Olyra’s deposition has independent authentication. Iria’s empty chair asks whether she will sit as curator, speak as a Vale, or surrender the museum seal. Captain Renn attends only to request an order.

Build the hearing from four kinds of proof. **Theft** needs the missing vow-bed plus a credible Vale transfer or Tavia’s admission. **Imminent danger** needs chapel notes, a live pin, or a demonstration that the peal can carry compulsion. **Independent authentication** comes from Senna’s chain, infirmary material, or authenticated House copies under a named custodian. **Public witness** requires two counter-signed court statements, a committed petitioner, or someone ready to speak in the chamber. Quality and custody matter. Four versions of one museum claim still count once.

Proof becomes authority in combinations. Theft plus a Vale destination yields a narrow recovery warrant. Danger plus authentication yields belfry inspection and a quarter-hour hold. Theft plus danger yields emergency manor entry and watch support, but no automatic publication. Authentication plus public witness enters the deposition and trustee response into the same-day council record. Any three combine warrant, hold, and record. All four divide the board and place Dorr’s obstruction beside the evidence. Once written, these outputs persist.

A refusal also travels. A denied warrant bears the rejected proof in Dorr’s hand. Renn can preserve the gallery and shadow the carriage without exceeding it. A lost cancellation demand may still win a hold, belfry inspection, or permission for the West Door families to withdraw. Covert records may fail formal authentication and still move Maelin or Corven. A confrontation may close the vault and open the chamber windows to the crowd.

Dorr did not build the rite. His fault is choosing controlled disclosure over the people who pay for delay. He can accept split custody, a timed public reading, a guarded search, or a warning pattern that preserves order without preserving silence. He rejects invented occult motives. Expose him, bargain with him, bypass him, or make him sign the refusal. A forum secured here matters to Edrin because it already holds records, witnesses, and custody; another private review does not.

**If skipped or reached late.** Dorr acts on reports that reach him. Without contrary evidence he orders containment, preserves the peal, and calls the rupture theft and vandalism. He cannot invent the archive or Tavia’s location. The other trustees keep their divisions. Every order, abstention, and limited inspection remains usable later. Once copies, witnesses, or a warning peal spread, even Dorr’s preferred hearing begins from public facts.

encounters.title: The West Infirmary
encounters.summary: A working hospice preserves Olyra’s defiance in doors, frames, cloth, and living terms no Vale or trustee may claim wholesale.
encounters.opening_view: “Not the glass,” Caldra Fen says, finishing a bandage. “The people who remember it.” Behind her, clear panes fill the shrine gaps above sleeping patients. The old fever doors preserve both commands: seal us in, cut us out. Survivor names cover one table, paired with questions for a saint who may answer in borrowed words. No family has signed away its testimony, relics, or grief.
encounters.content:
Sister Caldra Fen runs a working hospice in the surviving west wing. Its families are neither a single witness nor a chorus waiting to certify someone else’s case. Caldra controls patient access and the fever doors. Ilye Aven keeps the bed-frame tallies; she will authenticate names and leave the frames where patients use them. Tomar Ordel holds a family copy of Olyra’s final instructions and distrusts every Vale, Iria included. The Sorn line appears in the burial register. Tavia’s crime grants neither guilt nor authority to her relatives. Care continues while the city debates its dead.

The ward keeps evidence no archive can manufacture: names cut into bed frames, burial cloth marked by Olyra’s hand, the council order still nailed to one fever door, axe cuts opening the other from within, and histories maintained across households. Olyra opened the sealed infirmary, set the able patients to water and burial work, and died after the council refused reinforcement. Survivors built the first shrine here. Alis later moved its colored panes to the Vale winter garden “for protection.” Edrin recently measured the empty frames and asked whether the families would testify if the saint called them. Caldra answered in writing: they will testify for Olyra; they will not be commanded by her image.

Commitment costs labor and trust. Caldra speaks if another healer covers the ward and the record stays outside trustee and Vale custody. Ilye brings rubbings and the tally key, never the frames. Tomar reads the family copy if Iria acknowledges the concealment without asking forgiveness in the same breath. Two other families will sign but will not enter the court. Meet those terms to gain authentication, public witnesses, and a West Door delegation. Pressure patients, take objects, or promise vindication from the Glass Saint, and particular witnesses withdraw. The history remains.

Tavia may seek refuge here. If trustee seizure threatens the House, she brings the cut leaf because her ancestor’s name appears on it. Caldra will not hide her from a lawful public charge or hand her into a closed museum transfer. She insists that confession, leaf, and family testimony be heard together. Show Tavia the chapel’s vocal cost or Alis’s warning and she turns toward cooperation. Condemn Edrin alone and she remains unmoved; she already knows the theft was unlawful and judged silence worse.

The infirmary can authenticate the deposition, recruit witnesses, trace the shrine panes, reveal a maintenance route into the manor, and hold copies outside museum and Vale hands. Late in the day, ordinary window glass begins repeating nearby prayers. The fragments attack no one and answer nothing. They show the rite gathering the city’s language. Without investigator agreements, Ilye still sends a rubbing to Nessa Quill and Tomar still tells the West Door families the question has reopened. This place moves on its own terms.

**If skipped or reached late.** Names on a page create no promise of testimony, custody, or a breath-giver from Caldra. West Door families follow commitments already made in the court; otherwise they remain at the hospice or withdraw independently. The doors, copies, empty frames, and maintenance measurements remain. If a bell command reaches the ward, resolve what it does to patients and staff before treating the hospice as uncomplicated support.

encounters.title: The House of Petitions
encounters.summary: Petitioners expose the vow-bed’s contradictory language, judge Tavia’s confession, and decide how evidence will move through the city.
encounters.opening_view: A signed accusation reaches the rear copy window before its author reaches the front desk. Then another follows it. Shelves rise over cures, pardons, debts, births, disappearances, and refusals. Four caucuses argue across one table; copyists mark a warning-bell chart; petitioners press signed sheets into unfamiliar hands. Nessa Quill climbs onto a chair, not to quiet the room, but to keep every sheet moving while the doorway thickens.
encounters.content:
Nessa Quill keeps the House of Petitions, an independent copy office that preserves words before they are engraved, burned, or laid beneath civic relics. Four caucuses crowd the main room. The Open Hands seek cures, pardons, and debt relief; they want publication and a stopped peal. The Returned Names seek missing children, sailors, and soldiers; many would let Edrin make the saint answer. The West Door Circle keeps infirmary petitions and rejects both the obedience legend and compulsory command. The Quiet Keepers fear that street action will give Dorr cause to close the House. Nessa keeps sheets moving. She cannot make the room desire one ending.

The ledgers show that the vow-bed carries more than names. Its engravings repeat incompatible commands: obey lawful authority, protect children, punish betrayal, forgive debt, return the absent, make the city pure. Edrin tested mirrored silver against different petition sets; the figure’s language changed with the cards. Current copies can weight, contradict, or bound an answering form, but one afternoon cannot overwrite six decades of silver. The House therefore governs custody, witnesses, and hearing terms—not a cleanly authored command.

Tavia is a culpable witness in motion. If she arrives unopposed, she brings the cut archive leaf, a bloodied cuff, and Edrin’s order to distribute the record before sunset. In **Defiance**, she admits the theft to Nessa, refuses trustee custody, and withholds the manor service route while she tests whether the investigators mean to bury the pages. Proof of the vocal cost plus custody outside private trustee control moves her to **Cooperation**. She then gives the full transfer statement, names chapel deliveries and the service route, and helps issue a warning, expecting arrest afterward. Under Renn’s public seal she testifies. A closed transfer ordered by Dorr ends her cooperation. Threatened with private seizure, destroyed evidence, or summary violence, she **Flees** to the infirmary with the leaf. Left unpersuaded and uncornered, she distributes copies and later goes to the manor to demand publication before the bell. Sabotage, Lio’s injury, and theft remain hers in every state.

Choose how the pages travel. A **certified reading** joins Senna’s or Caldra’s authentication to Nessa’s copy and creates a hearing Edrin may trust. A **distributed packet** places deposition, trustee minute, and witness statements with several keepers; suppression becomes difficult and rumor accelerates. A **public-custody pledge** names the future holders of records and recovered silver. A **warning assembly** sends petitioners toward belfry or manor, creating witnesses and crowd pressure. A **quiet escrow** protects records while yielding Dorr the first public account.

A seizure order begins a scene. The Quiet Keepers may divide from the other caucuses. Renn can reject private confiscation if the House names custodians and holds no stolen object. Investigators may negotiate split custody, pass copies through rear windows, read the order aloud, or defend the building. Violence wins paper and confirms Edrin’s belief that testimony receives force. If the House fractures, each caucus carries a piece elsewhere: Open Hands to the court, Returned Names toward the manor, West Door Circle to the infirmary, Quiet Keepers into private storage. Failure disperses the route; it never deletes it.

**If skipped or reached late.** Tavia gives Nessa the cut leaf and names the voice risk only if that knowledge has reached her. Open Hands begin public copies, Returned Names carry one packet toward the manor, West Door Circle sends one to the infirmary, and Quiet Keepers hide one off-site. Current petitions enter no apparatus by themselves; someone must carry and place them. A late group finds a constituency distributed across named destinations.

encounters.title: The Bell Chapel
encounters.summary: A rehearsal already speaking in borrowed voices reveals body, mouth, and reach; strip, cord, and deposition can answer the peal at different costs.
encounters.opening_view: The first word spoken in the chapel returns in a glass voice. No bell moves. Ropes narrow the nave; petition cards command from the floor; fresh wax binds a Vale ribbon into a mouth-shaped knot. A severed strand crosses the chalk road from museum to belfry to winter garden. Above, the practice clapper slips. Every rope answers.
encounters.content:
Edrin chose the chapel because its bell once called attendants to the west infirmary. The rehearsal has been left speaking. Four workings cross the nave: a mirrored frame over interchangeable petition cards; a mouth knot tied around a Vale hair ribbon; a relay board with six pin-shaped recesses; and a chalk route joining the Grand Belfry, East Gate, River Ward, and Vale Manor. Five intact pins appear on the plan. Cracked wax marks the spent museum trigger. The three Grand Belfry recesses read **witness**, **mouth**, and **crown**; the lesser towers read **relay**. Relay pins repeat the crown note. They cannot make the body or take a voice.

The rehearsal still answers. Exchange the petition cards and hand-sized glass attendants recite incompatible civic virtues. Put a hand inside the mouth knot and the nearest figure borrows the last sentence spoken in the room. Strike the relay board and the chapel bell answers without moving; one listener feels a sharp urge to obey the clearest imperative just heard. The figures fail to recognize Edrin, Olyra’s doors, or the same childhood memory twice. These tests separate language, voice, range, and instability. Let investigators stop after one proof, press for more certainty, or dismantle the workshop. Each additional test risks another line, pin, or spoken command.

The room punishes careless position. Waxed ropes tighten under crossed weight. A live pin snaps toward nearby bell metal. A cut tie drops the practice clapper through the nave. The wrong line sends a pulse that steals one complete sentence from the nearest speaker and gives it to the figures until the next bell note. Colored sleeves, tie-offs, and Edrin’s safe order reward a careful search. Tavia’s shorthand in the margin records the museum cut. Bell training, patient trials, or two workers approaching from opposite sides permit controlled dismantling. A rush still yields evidence, but may leave a pin live, damage one counterkey part, or preserve the investigators’ last imperative in the rehearsal.

The **counterkey** answers the rite in three pieces. The notched tuning strip identifies a live pin and lets a gloved hand lift it without carrying the vibration into the bell. The braided reversal cord changes a command knot into a confined or answering knot. The pitch table aligns those forms with the three long notes and the necessary lines of Olyra’s deposition. Strip alone: safe pin removal. Cord plus table: retuning. All three, Olyra’s text, and a willing breath-giver: bounded answering. A damaged set narrows the work; each surviving part keeps its listed use.

Every answer changes what the city will hear. Silence the witness bell and no body forms, but the procession loses its opening cadence. Lift the mouth pin after the first note and the glass body remains voiceless. Lift or mute the crown and the manor remains dangerous while the city escapes command. Retune the outer knot and confine the third note to everyone in the winter garden. Turn it outward into an answering form and a willing speaker lends one breath per answer, risking muteness until dawn. Remove the vow-bed and the speaking body collapses while the heartglass survives. Break the heartglass and every manifestation ends with Olyra’s last material relic.

Take any subset of tools, notes, and witnessed demonstrations. Record what survives, who saw each test, whether a sentence was stolen, and whether a practice pin remains live. Jori Kest can verify only what reaches him. Dorr can dismiss only what remains unsupported.

**If skipped or reached late.** Edrin does not return for the counterkey. Strip, cord, and table remain where Edrin left them until someone carries them out. The belfry can brake or damage a known bell without the set, but cannot safely lift live pins or retune with control. After the witness note, mouth and crown work still matters. After the mouth note, crown and warning work still matters. A late search yields the tools for the stages still ahead.

encounters.title: The Grand Belfry
encounters.summary: Every rope is a public choice: the divided ringers can silence, confine, warn, or carry the rite, and bronze remembers what they do.
encounters.opening_view: Six ropes descend through the crew, three answer-pins humming among them. Jori Kest holds Dorr’s sealed order. Mela Fen strikes the locked wheel-loft door once from above. “First lift,” calls Rian Voss. “Full peal,” answers Karel Venn. The counterweight rises through their disagreement, hauling every command toward bronze. Nobody has released a rope; nobody has agreed what the city is about to hear.
encounters.content:
The Grand Belfry carries the three long notes and keeps two lesser towers in time. Name every hand on a rope before the first lift. Bellmaster **Jori Kest** directs the room and will not gamble a ringer on an unexplained device. Crown ringer **Rian Voss** treats Dorr’s sealed order as the crew’s only shield. Silver-bell ringer **Mela Fen** found an intruder in the wheel loft and locked herself on the crown deck with the tuning ledger. Juniors **Pavo Tern** and **Lis Aven** hold tie-offs, carry messages, and may flee when fear outruns discipline. The intruder, **Karel Venn** of the Returned Names, is trying to preserve the full peal because he believes delay will bury the record again. Edrin never sent him. Rumor did.

The tower stacks its dangers across three floors. The ringing room holds ropes, brakes, Dorr’s order, and the warning chart. The wheel loft holds moving wheels, counterweights, and the live stage pins. The crown deck holds the bell mouths, Mela, the ledger, and sight lines to the court and relay towers. Once a bell moves, its rope lane can lift, drag, or strike anyone who crosses it. A loose counterweight can take the loft stairs. Bare metal against a humming pin carries its imperative resonance into the next bell. Position, stopped machinery, crew control, and tie-offs decide the danger.

The **witness pin** on the west tenor carries the first note and raises the reflected body at Vale Manor. The **mouth pin** on the silver bell carries the second and opens the nearest Vale as its speaker. The **crown pin** launches the command. East Gate and River Ward relay only a crown note that reaches them. Lift the crown pin and the city is safe even if body and voice stages occur. Lift all three and the Grand Belfry drives none of the rite. Dorr may move ceremonial music to the lesser towers; relay pins cannot begin the sequence.

Kest needs something he can put before his crew. The chapel strip identifies a linked pin set. The pitch table and Mela’s ledger match stages to bells. A warrant, inspection order, or signed hold gives legal cover. Named petitioners or infirmary witnesses give public cover. Tavia’s statement proves deliberate sabotage. One technical proof plus lawful or public protection is enough for controlled work. Without it, seizure remains possible, but Rian calls the watch, a junior may run, and Dorr can name the intervention as a second attack.

Choose what the bells will be allowed to do. **Strip all stage pins:** stop all three bells, secure the loft, and use the strip; every stage fails, the full peal is lost, and the crew is publicly implicated. **Lift the crown:** one controlled ascent prevents city-wide command while leaving body and voice danger at the manor. **Mute or bind one bell:** fast without the counterkey, dangerous under motion, and visible as sabotage; that stage remains silent until repaired. **Retune the sequence:** reversal cord, pitch table, Mela’s ledger, Kest or equivalent skill, and two cooperative ringers confine the crown note to the winter garden while preserving the first two. **Sound the warning:** two ringers and an intact warning bell draw watch, petitioners, and witnesses toward the manor; concealment ends, panic may begin. **Preserve the peal:** an informed choice for bounded answering or accepted risk.

A sounded note cannot be unsounded; every later note remains contestable. Before the witness note, every operation stands. After it, mouth, crown, retuning, and warning remain. After the mouth note, the Vale voice is already gone, but crown removal still protects the city and retuning still confines the command. Once the crown starts, braking the bell, breaking the pin, or severing the rope may reduce the relays; no action recalls a sounded command. Record lifted pins, cut ropes, convinced ringers, injuries, warnings, and orders shown. Dorr can send officers and new paper. He cannot instantly restore bronze, trust, or rigging.

**If skipped entirely.** Kest follows Dorr’s peal order because no proof or protection reaches him. Rian readies the crown rope, Mela stays locked above, Karel works to preserve the full peal, and Pavo or Lis carries any order that actually arrives. When manor and crew are ready, intact stage pins sound in order. No warning sounds by default. Later testimony, pin placement, and consequences remain. Skipping the tower accelerates the rite; it erases nothing.

encounters.title: Vale Manor
encounters.summary: At the winter garden, every copied page, opened door, altered bell, willing witness, and surviving pane determines what Edrin can still make speak.
encounters.opening_view: “You came before the bells,” Edrin Vale says. He stands inside the winter garden’s rope circle with the stolen silver beneath the suspended heartglass and an open dossier at his feet. Old shrine panes cast faces across the servants, the doors, and the witnesses gathering beyond the wall. One hand rests on the inner knot. Under the floor, the bell trunk gives a low tremor, and every pane returns a different face.
encounters.content:
Before Edrin speaks, read the city already gathered at the glass. Record the surviving stage and relay pins, any warning pattern, the procession’s position, the holders of authenticated copies, Captain Renn’s exact authority, witnesses and petitioners in motion, Tavia’s state, and whether Iria accompanies the investigators. A cut rope, public copy, signed denial, dispersed crowd, or lifted pin stays changed when the scene moves.

**Six ways through the doors.** A recovery or emergency-entry warrant brings Renn and four officers through the carriage gate. Its written scope protects servants, seals objects, and restrains named suspects; it also defines the overreach Dorr may later allege. Iria may claim the east door. Steward **Leva Orm** admits her and companions who accept a household inventory, while Iria’s presence creates a second possible Vale speaker. Tavia knows the laundry court and silver-pantry route to the garden side passage and vow-bed braces; covert speed costs public legitimacy unless someone outside knows the purpose. Infirmary measurements reveal a maintenance passage beneath the shrine frames, opening beside the bell trunk and four foundation anchors. A warning peal or petitioner march crosses the west lawn in public; Edrin opens the garden doors so the record cannot vanish, and the crowd brings crush, custody, and command risk. Direct force through doors, roof, or panes remains possible. It alarms the household and turns controlled glass and rope into falling hazards.

**The household at the glass.** Edrin begins on the speaker mark, dossier open, heartglass above the vow-bed, one hand on the mouth line. He takes no hostages and orders no servant to fight. Leva waits in the front hall with keys, servant roll, and a blank inventory. She wants the concealment ended and the coercive rite stopped. A lawful order, Iria’s acknowledgment, or proof of involuntary voice loss moves her into evacuation and active inventory. Indiscriminate violence makes her bar doors and protect people. Garden keeper and glazier **Peren Holt** waits beside the pane latches in the undercroft. Edrin promised a public display, not command. Show Peren a live mouth effect or Tavia’s account and he releases shutters, unseats panes, or guides investigators through the maintenance passage. Without proof he protects the old glass. Six servants remain in the detached kitchen court as witnesses and people to evacuate, never reserve combatants.

**Five joined things give the saint a body.** The **pane crown** mounts eight shrine panes in hinged iron frames. Open panes admit procession light and public reflections; shutters and released frames weaken the body and narrow what it can mirror. The **vow-bed table** holds the engraved silver and any current petitions placed during play. Remove, cover, or replace those words to change the available language; wrenching the bed free after manifestation throws sharp reflected phrases through the room. The **heartglass cradle** suspends Olyra’s relic over the silver. Lower and seal it to end a formed body. Break it to end every stage and Olyra’s last material link. The **inner mouth knot** marks the speaker circle. When the mouth note completes, the nearest living Vale inside the outer pane circle loses their natural voice. Edrin begins nearest. Iria becomes the target only by entering or remaining after he is moved beyond the circle. The mouth stage fails without either a Vale inside or a hand closing the inner line. The **bell trunk** carries witness, mouth, and crown vibrations under the floor. Tie off an unsounded branch from the undercroft; a sounded branch is history.

**Edrin listens only for a hearing that already exists.** Edrin begins in **Declaration**. He admits theft and sabotage, displays the dossier, and says the museum forfeited the right to choose its own hearing. One public anchor—a same-day council entry, certified records outside Vale and museum custody, named witnesses present or audibly assembling, a warning peal, or petitioners reading the deposition—moves him to **Pause** before the witness note. He hears exact terms and allows inspection; Dorr’s sealed promise still means nothing. Two independent anchors plus named custody for heartglass, vow-bed, and dossier move him to **Witnessed Terms**. He opens the outer knot, leaves the speaker mark, and negotiates surrender, public reading, or bounded answering. Tavia’s public rejection of the vocal cost, Iria’s acknowledgment, and Jori’s certification alter his posture but do not replace custody. Private seizure, destroyed copies, or an unannounced assault moves him to **Hardened Assembly**. He closes doors and advances the next available trigger, without taking hostages or attacking a surrendered witness. New public facts can move him back to Pause even after the body forms.

Move Edrin only when pages, witnesses, custody, or altered glass make his next position untenable. Ask what has become public, who holds each object, and which promise survives tomorrow’s change of office or family mind.

**The three notes borrow body, voice, and reach in order.** Before the **witness note**, inventory, negotiation, sealed custody, zone-by-zone dismantling, and reversal all remain possible. An intact witness pin casts light from the panes across the vow-bed and raises a translucent human outline. It recites incompatible petition fragments and civic virtues. It answers no question and recognizes no relic. The body persists while heartglass, silver, and four pane frames remain joined. Remove the heartglass, separate the bed, or release enough frames to collapse it.

An intact **mouth note** completed while Edrin closes the knot takes the nearest living Vale’s natural voice. The body speaks in that timbre without the speaker’s will or memory. Move a Vale before completion to change the target; carrying the speaker away afterward does not restore the voice. Cut or reverse the knot before completion to prevent involuntary transfer. With all three counterkey parts, Olyra’s deposition, a willing breath-giver, and witnessed consent, tie the reversal cord outward. The answering form borrows breath until dawn, remains inside the garden, and answers at most three questions from records and petitions physically present. It reveals no unknown fact, hidden culprit, or proof that it is Olyra. Uncertainty comes as contradiction, silence, or an irrelevant petition.

An intact **crown note** takes its range from the belfry record. No crown pin, no launched command. A retuned crown confines it to the winter garden. One relay reaches its connected wards; two reach the procession route. Derive its language from three streams recorded before arrival: the vow-bed’s old engravings, current petitions physically added, and the phrase most publicly repeated by Edrin, petitioners, trustees, or investigators. A phrase supported by two streams governs. If all three conflict, the intact vow-bed’s most repeated civic formula governs unless deliberately covered or altered. Use a short command whose ordinary readings produce aid and danger. The body speaks only from the recorded streams; it cannot settle Olyra’s meaning.

**Every command opens one door and breaks another.** “Open the doors” frees sealed wards and records while opening prisons, sickrooms, homes, and dangerous works. “Speak the names” restores suppressed victims and exposes protected identities, accusations, and private grief. “Forgive the debts” breaks predatory claims and also wages, care obligations, restitution, and common stores. “Return them” sends people after family, fugitives, exiles, and the dead. “Protect the children” produces shelter, abduction, family conflict, and violent paternalism. “Obey the wounded” centers neglected testimony and grants contradictory demands coercive force. Derive any new command from established language and name at least one aid and one danger before it sounds.

**What survives decides the ending.** **Witnessed surrender** preserves the apparatus under split custody and sends Edrin to prosecution without manifestation. **Dismantling before the witness note** prevents supernatural evidence while leaving the documentary dispute. **Bounded answering** yields up to three composite replies, temporary muteness, and a contested public source. **Witness-only manifestation** creates observers without stolen voice or command. **Voice taken, crown stopped** leaves one Vale mute unless restored before dawn and protects the city. A **confined command** reaches garden and west lawn; a **partial relay** divides East Gate from River Ward; a **full awakening** compels the procession until dawn. **Heartglass destruction** ends the body and may leave a taken voice unrestored. **Violent failure** follows the damaged zone: falling panes, trapped bodies, broken silver, or one surviving relay.

Write the ending on separate lines: body formed; voice taken; command and range; condition and custodian of heartglass, vow-bed, panes, counterkey, and dossier; witnesses to each stage; injuries, detentions, and commitments.

**Before dawn, the stolen voice may choose return.** An involuntary transfer outlives the figure. The original speaker may consent in writing to a reversed mouth working before dawn. It needs intact heartglass, reversal cord, mouth-pitch cue, and one independent witness. Seal the heartglass over an empty or covered vow-bed, tie the inner line outward, and let the speaker choose whether to reclaim the voice. Success returns it and leaves the heartglass acoustically inert. Destroyed heartglass, lost cord, dawn, or refusal makes the muteness lasting. Edrin’s surrender restores nothing by itself.

**After the bells, the city keeps five reckonings.** **Custody:** name a holder and access rule for every surviving object; split custody may include watch, infirmary, House, museum, or a new trust. **Publication:** distinguish council entry, witnessed reading, distributed dispute, and resealed originals; spoken or copied knowledge persists. **Prosecution:** Edrin answers for conspiracy, receiving stolen civic property, and attempted compulsion; Tavia for sabotage, Lio’s injury, theft, and evidence removal, with cooperation and prevented harm as mitigation; Dorr and participating trustees for concealment and obstruction; Iria politically and professionally for what she knew, withheld, certified, or disclosed. **Surviving compulsion:** mark affected rooms or wards, concrete emergencies, and the institutions responding before dawn. **Olyra’s memory:** record what is authenticated, disputed, fractured, memorialized, exhibited, or managed into another silence.

End when immediate coercion and physical danger are resolved. Close with named custody, testimony, accusations, and one visible public consequence. The city may finally know that Olyra opened the west doors without agreeing what her defiance asks of it now.

revelations.title: The shattered gallery still contains the sabotage’s missing step
revelations.description: Evidence elsewhere redirects the investigators to the outward rupture, the removed silver vow-bed, Tavia’s service-door route, and the moment the theft passed into public view.

revelations.title: The archive proves the public relic was false and the true heartglass remained with the Vales
revelations.description: Restricted records join the substitution, Olyra’s deposition, the trustees’ recent concealment, and the silver vessel engraved by decades of public petitions.

revelations.title: The bell chapel reveals the awakening’s construction, cost, and countermeasures
revelations.description: Edrin rehearsed a six-pin bell network whose separate stages form a body, take a Vale mouth, and launch a relayed command; the chapel’s three-part counterkey permits partial, late, and costly interference.

revelations.title: Edrin is assembling the heartglass and stolen vow-bed at Vale Manor
revelations.description: The winter garden’s old shrine panes complete the apparatus, making the manor the place to stop, redirect, bargain over, or permit the manifestation.

revelations.title: The procession court holds the theft’s public witnesses and broken transfer route
revelations.description: Tavia moved the silver bed through the rehearsal crowd, changed carriers, and left witnesses who saw different parts of the handoff.

revelations.title: The trustees’ chamber can turn evidence into a warrant, delay, public record, or obstruction
revelations.description: Provost Dorr and the trustees control lawful access and the procession schedule, but public evidence can divide or bind them.

revelations.title: The west infirmary preserves the people, objects, and testimony erased from Olyra’s civic legend
revelations.description: The fever doors, survivor records, shrine frames, and living hospice authenticate Olyra’s defiance outside Vale or museum custody.

revelations.title: The House of Petitions knows what the stolen silver has accumulated and where Tavia fled
revelations.description: Copy ledgers and living petitioners reveal the vow-bed’s command language, while Tavia brings the stolen archive leaf there.

revelations.title: The Grand Belfry controls whether the final command reaches the city
revelations.description: Three stage pins in the Grand Belfry drive the rite and two lesser towers only relay its crown note; the crew can strip, mute, retune, warn through, defend, or preserve that configuration.

revelations.title: The city made Olyra a saint of the obedience she died refusing
revelations.description: Olyra opened the sealed infirmary against council orders; later sermons preserved her authority by reversing the meaning of her death.

revelations.title: Tavia Sorn removed the vow-bed for Edrin and carried the record toward the petitioners
revelations.description: The assistant conservator planned the rupture and transfer but separated from Edrin to publish evidence before the rite.

revelations.title: The vow-bed turns six decades of petitions into the manifestation’s available language
revelations.description: The silver carries incompatible requests and civic commands; current petition copies can weight or bound the result but cannot make it reliable.

revelations.title: The Glass Saint will be a composite witness, not Olyra restored
revelations.description: Rehearsals change with the supplied petitions and fail to preserve a stable personality, memory, or answer.

revelations.title: The second bell takes a Vale voice and the third broadcasts one compelling command
revelations.description: Edrin expects to lose his voice, but the cost can shift to Iria; answer-fitted bells carry the command until dawn.

revelations.title: Edrin will pause for a public hearing already made credible, not another promise of review
revelations.description: Protected records, named witnesses, a council entry, petitioners, or a warning peal can prove that surrender will not return the truth to private custody.

revelations.title: The procession peal can be delayed, muted, or retuned without settling the relic’s fate
revelations.description: Bell access and the chapel working set can prevent individual stages, stop city-wide relay, confine the third note, or preserve an informed answering attempt, even after an earlier note has sounded.

clues.title: Accession number beneath the painted bone copy
clues.description: The number belongs to a restricted substitution ledger rather than the public catalogue.

clues.title: Bell-metal filings beneath the burst case
clues.description: Fresh bronze filings and chapel wax identify an answer-pin tuned at the abandoned bell chapel.

clues.title: Vale carriage seal in the packing felt
clues.description: A torn strip from the missing silver bed bears the wax seal of a private Vale carriage.

clues.title: Fresh Vale wax on the replacement wagon strap
clues.description: Hara Bex found the wagon’s cut strap replaced with one sealed from a Vale carriage moments before Edrin’s coach left for the manor.

clues.title: Tavia’s winter-garden service-route sketch
clues.description: When she cooperates, Tavia marks the laundry court and silver-pantry passage used to carry the vow-bed into the manor’s winter garden.

clues.title: Conservation memorandum for the silver vow-bed
clues.description: The memorandum records the engraved silver support now missing from the shattered gallery.

clues.title: Restorer’s bell-and-window diagram
clues.description: A marginal sketch matches the bell chapel’s rope geometry to panes in the Vale winter garden.

clues.title: Private transfer ledger for the true heartglass
clues.description: The authentic relic was retained at Vale Manor, where Edrin recently inspected its case.

clues.title: Marked museum extraction plan
clues.description: The route begins beneath the shattered case and ends at the carriage door used during the panic.

clues.title: Copied folio naming the substitution ledger
clues.description: Edrin’s copy cites the restricted shelf that records the false display and Vale custody.

clues.title: Winter-garden peal sequence
clues.description: The notes place the completed apparatus at Vale Manor and time its three stages to sunset bells.

clues.title: Crate holding the museum’s silver vow-bed
clues.description: Fresh museum packing marks and cut fasteners identify the component removed from the gallery.

clues.title: Stolen provenance and deposition dossier
clues.description: The dossier bears the archive vault’s restricted stamp and contains Olyra’s censored accusation.

clues.title: Bell-rope counterkey beside the apparatus
clues.description: The coded knot sequence matches the chapel rehearsal and can reverse the rite’s commanding form.

clues.title: Docent’s service-door witness line
clues.description: The docent saw a museum cloak carry a flat wrapped weight toward the public court during the rupture.

clues.title: Petition-wagon transfer note
clues.description: A copyist recorded the wagon number and the moment Tavia changed the silver bed to Edrin’s carriage.

clues.title: Bell-tower view of the court
clues.description: From the west louver, a ringer saw the grey cloak, petition wagon, and Vale carriage converge below.

clues.title: Dorr’s summons to the emergency session
clues.description: A deputy carries orders naming the trustees’ chamber as the place where evidence and procession delays will be judged.

clues.title: Modern trustee concealment minute
clues.description: The signed minute records Dorr’s vote to postpone publication until after the procession.

clues.title: Council seal on the peal order
clues.description: Kest’s order identifies Dorr and the chamber as the authority preserving the full peal.

clues.title: West infirmary name on the copy backing
clues.description: A conservation label says the devotional copy was modeled on a shrine once kept at the west infirmary.

clues.title: Survivor index beside the deposition
clues.description: The archive index directs authenticators to bed-frame tallies and family copies still kept at the hospice.

clues.title: Dorr’s dismissal of hospice testimony
clues.description: Dorr calls Caldra Fen and the survivor families interested witnesses, confirming where independent testimony can be found.

clues.title: Tavia’s copyist token
clues.description: The token dropped with her cloak grants after-hours entry to the House of Petitions.

clues.title: Trustee seizure order for petition ledgers
clues.description: A draft order names the house and its copied inscriptions as evidence Dorr wants secured before rumor spreads.

clues.title: Family-copy ledger address
clues.description: The hospice’s survivor index names Nessa Quill as keeper of the petition copies tied to infirmary families.

clues.title: Answer-pin installation order
clues.description: A routine maintenance order sent three unexplained pins to the Grand Belfry under Edrin’s conservation authorization.

clues.title: Copyists’ warning pattern
clues.description: The petitioners know the public warning sequence and the name of the bellmaster who can sound it.

clues.title: Grand Belfry mark on the ritual map
clues.description: The chalk map identifies three stage pins in the Grand Belfry and relay pins at East Gate and River Ward; only the crown pin launches the city-wide command.

clues.title: Crown bell named on the marshal’s cue sheet
clues.description: The rehearsal order assigns the three long notes to the Grand Belfry and lists East Gate and River Ward only as followers of its crown cue.

clues.title: Tavia’s restricted-shelf slip
clues.description: A folded request in her cloak names the restricted substitution ledger and its shelf mark.

clues.title: Chapel knot copied in the hospice letter
clues.description: Edrin’s letter sketches the same outer knot now fixed across the abandoned chapel floor.

clues.title: Vale maintenance route in the shrine frame
clues.description: Measurements on the empty frame match a service door beneath the manor winter garden.

clues.title: Chapel delivery receipt
clues.description: Tavia paid a copyist to carry wax, petition cards, and bell cord to the abandoned chapel.

clues.title: Manor warning signal in the bell log
clues.description: A private signal added to the peal schedule is carried by a named Vale runner and tells Edrin when the procession has entered range of the winter garden.

clues.title: Olyra’s deposition beneath the broken seal
clues.description: The deposition states that Olyra opened the infirmary after the council ordered everyone inside abandoned.

clues.title: Axe cuts on the fever door
clues.description: The cuts run from the inside out and survivor names identify Olyra among those who broke the seal.

clues.title: Official sermon beside a family petition
clues.description: The sermon praises obedience while the family petition thanks Olyra for refusing the council order.

clues.title: Trustees’ language of order
clues.description: Dorr repeats the same formula of lawful patience used in the later sermons, exposing what the legend was built to protect.

clues.title: Censored accusation in the stolen dossier
clues.description: Olyra’s own charge against the council is bound behind donor correspondence that later praises her obedience, making the reversal visible in one seized packet.

clues.title: Missing conservator’s saw
clues.description: Tavia’s numbered saw matches the two clean cuts beneath the missing silver bed.

clues.title: Copyists’ handoff testimony
clues.description: Two copyists heard Tavia argue with Edrin before the silver changed carriages.

clues.title: Tavia’s bloodied museum cuff
clues.description: The cuff carries gallery glass, silver filings, and her written account of the planned transfer.

clues.title: Cut leaf matched to Tavia’s shelf request
clues.description: The missing edge fits the leaf Tavia carried away, and her access slip places her in the restricted ledger before the gallery rupture.

clues.title: Tavia’s conservation shorthand on the cutting order
clues.description: The safe sequence for loosening the museum mount and moving the silver is annotated in Tavia’s hand beside Edrin’s ritual notes.

clues.title: Engraved petition ghosts in the packing felt
clues.description: Pressure marks preserve overlapping commands once engraved into the missing silver.

clues.title: Six decades of copy ledgers
clues.description: The ledgers show recurring commands and incompatible requests accumulated beneath the relic.

clues.title: Petition-swapped rehearsal figures
clues.description: Glass figures repeat different virtues when the cards beneath their mirrored frame are exchanged.

clues.title: Silver bed speaking in layers
clues.description: Before the first bell, phrases from old engravings whisper from different parts of the assembled silver.

clues.title: Hospice glass repeats nearby prayers
clues.description: After the rite begins gathering language, ordinary panes answer with fragments spoken beside them, proving that the manifestation feeds on current public words as well as old engraving.

clues.title: Infirmary memory the relic lacks
clues.description: Caldra asks test questions drawn from survivor testimony that Edrin’s rehearsal notes never answer consistently.

clues.title: Contradictory rehearsal transcripts
clues.description: Four test records change with petition cards, borrowed sentences, and spoken imperatives; no figure preserves a stable identity or account.

clues.title: Heartglass reflection fails to recognize the fever doors
clues.description: When shown a copied door image, the forming figure repeats a civic slogan instead of Olyra’s recorded words.

clues.title: Alis calls the heartglass a family witness
clues.description: A donor letter warns that the glass repeats whatever the household and petition silver bring to it; it preserves no complete mind of Olyra.

clues.title: Vale hair ribbon in the mouth knot
clues.description: The ritual diagram labels the nearest Vale body as the voice offered at the second note.

clues.title: Answer-pins resonate with spoken orders
clues.description: The witness, mouth, and crown pins hum at different pitches; a relay pin answers only when the crown pitch enters adjacent bell metal.

clues.title: Alis Vale’s warning in the transfer letter
clues.description: Alis wrote that the shrine glass could make a family voice “common property” when rung through the city.

clues.title: Edrin’s written consent to silence
clues.description: Edrin has signed a statement accepting permanent loss of speech without accounting for Iria’s proximity.

clues.title: Dorr’s public-record threshold
clues.description: The council procedure shows exactly how protected copies and named witnesses can force a same-day entry.

clues.title: Caldra’s conditional testimony
clues.description: Caldra will testify if the records remain outside Vale and trustee custody.

clues.title: Petitioners’ public-custody pledge
clues.description: Nessa offers signed copies, named keepers, and a public reading before the procession reaches the manor.

clues.title: Edrin’s draft surrender terms
clues.description: The unsigned terms demand immediate publication, protected witnesses, and custody outside the museum.

clues.title: Counter-signed custody copy outside the museum
clues.description: Lio’s statement and Ossa’s numbered inventory can be copied under the witness charter before trustee sealing, leaving a named public packet that no Vale or trustee can privately recall.

clues.title: Six-week publication deferral
clues.description: The trustees had already accepted the finding as credible and still postponed release until after the procession, showing why another private promise of review will not satisfy Edrin.

clues.title: Warning peal creates a public anchor
clues.description: Kest’s chart names the pattern that summons watch, petitioners, and witnesses to Vale Manor; once sounded, Edrin can hear that a public hearing already exists outside trustee control.

clues.title: Outer-knot timing table
clues.description: The table pairs the notched tuning strip, braided reversal cord, and deposition pitches with delayed, confined, and answering forms of the three-note sequence.

clues.title: Kest’s three-bell options
clues.description: Kest identifies the exact ropes, tie-offs, crew, and counterkey pieces required to strip the stage pins, lift only the crown pin, or retune the third note.

clues.title: Rehearsal order with a missed beat
clues.description: A prior rehearsal log shows that one missed crown-bell beat delayed every lesser tower without stopping the procession.

clues.title: Quarter-hour hold and belfry inspection order
clues.description: The chamber can suspend the crown cue and authorize a tower inspection without deciding custody of the relic or the truth of Olyra’s history.

events.title: What the Glass Threw Out
events.attendance_note: All four independent witnesses present under Iria Vale’s emergency charter.
events.opening_note: The Counterseal Witnesses enter a sealed museum scene while Dorr presses to classify the rupture as ordinary vandalism.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Iria Vale, Ors Renn, Ossa Pell, and Lio Marr

events.text: Mira and Ossa separate the answer-pin, theft tools, and destination evidence into three custody packets instead of treating the burst case as one undifferentiated scene.
Aven takes a counter-signed rubbing of the accession number; Renn seals the original shard and the missing-saw tray before Dorr can move them under an undocumented trustee order.
Lysa records Lio’s service-door sight line after Pell stabilizes the hanging case and clears glass from the docent’s path.

events.note: The restricted accession number makes the substitution ledger an actionable lead.
The bell-metal filings and chapel wax identify a workshop tied to the rupture, though the group does not yet know its full function.
The Vale carriage seal gives an immediate destination for direct pursuit.
Lio saw the wrapped weight enter the public court, where the transfer can be reconstructed from independent witnesses.
The copy backing identifies the west infirmary as an independent source for the original shrine and Olyra’s history.
Tavia’s missing numbered saw matches the cuts, making her the named theft suspect rather than merely the absent employee.

events.text: Renn holds the live answer-pin under watch seal; Ossa holds the saw tray; Aven carries a counter-signed accession rubbing outside trustee custody.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Sergeant Vela Rusk, Pellen Vey, Hara Bex, Iven Quill, and Sera Mott

events.text: The witnesses are interviewed separately: Pellen supplies weight, Hara supplies wax and wagon movement, and the copyists supply the argument and carriage handoff.
The group does not chase Tavia. Iven and Sera carry word to the House that the investigators will bring a certified record and evidence of a possible living cost.
Lysa asks the West Door families only to preserve their own observations; they withdraw their children from the front rank but make no promise to testify or accept custody.

events.note: Dorr’s summons identifies the chamber as the place where lawful scope and procession delay will be contested.
Tavia’s token identifies the House as her destination and the likely public-copy route.

events.text: Pellen, Hara, Iven, and Sera sign separate statements; the Vale-carriage allegation is public but remains disputed; the procession loses its West Door children from the front rank.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Senna Drail, Eren Sol, and Mave Kitt

events.text: Aven prioritizes the Olyra and modern-suppression packets. Eren certifies the deposition and survivor index while Mave certifies the trustee minute and recent conservation finding.
One certified set goes under Renn’s watch seal; one remains with the investigators for a public reading. Senna keeps every original and logs Dorr’s later suspension order.
The group deliberately leaves the ritual diagram packet unopened when Dorr’s order reaches the public stair; this preserves authentication but costs them the chapel-to-manor working details.

events.note: The memorandum confirms that the missing silver in the gallery is the object named by the old accession chain.
Olyra’s deposition directly states that she broke the council seal and opened the abandoned infirmary.
Alis’s warning establishes a real Vale voice hazard and city-wide transmission, but not yet the exact three-stage mechanism.

events.text: Two certified packets now exist outside Vale and museum control; Dorr’s signed suspension closes the public stair after their removal and enters Senna’s custody log.

events.closing_note: The witnesses have a theft route, a certified historical contradiction, and a living-voice warning, but no warrant, no counterkey, and no control of the sunset peal.

events.title: A Warrant Refused
events.attendance_note: All four independent witnesses present under Iria Vale’s emergency charter.
events.opening_note: The group brings certified evidence into the emergency trustee session while the procession resumes forming below the windows.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Helian Dorr, Iria Vale, Ors Renn, and the divided trustees

events.text: Dorr accepts that theft and concealment are proven but refuses a manor search and full procession delay, claiming the voice warning is too old and unspecific for private entry.
Renn obtains only a narrow belfry safety inspection. Dorr signs the refusal, preserves the full peal order, and orders petition copies held rather than destroyed.
Iria publicly acknowledges the false display and family custody but does not claim authority to surrender the heartglass or excuse Edrin.

events.note: The maintenance order identifies three unexplained Grand Belfry pins installed under Edrin’s authority.
The chamber procedure defines a same-day public entry and named custody plan that can survive another private promise.

events.text: Dorr denies the manor warrant and procession hold in writing, grants a narrow belfry inspection, preserves the full peal, and creates a signed public record of institutional refusal.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Nessa Quill, Tavia Sorn, and the four petition caucuses

events.text: Tavia reads Alis’s voice warning and rejects Edrin’s plan to take any Vale voice. She confesses sabotage, theft, and the carriage transfer without asking to be absolved.
Nessa sends certified copies through three named keepers and organizes a public reading outside Vale Manor. The Quiet Keepers retain one sealed copy rather than joining the march.
The most repeated current petition is “Open the doors,” but no one carries that packet into the winter garden. It becomes public language, not an automatic change to the vow-bed.

events.note: The copy ledgers show that the silver carries recurring, incompatible imperatives accumulated over decades.

events.text: Tavia cooperates under Renn’s named custody; three certified copy sets leave by different keepers; petitioners commit to a public reading outside the manor; no current petition packet is placed in the apparatus.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Jori Kest, Mela Fen, Rian Voss, Pavo Tern, Lis Aven, and Karel Venn

events.text: The group has no tuning strip and does not pretend otherwise. Pell and Kest identify the crown bell from Mela’s ledger and the pins’ separate resonance, then choose a manual rope bind instead of live-pin removal.
The narrow inspection order and Tavia’s confession give Kest enough cover for controlled work. Rian refuses to remove a pin but accepts a brake-post bind that can be inspected and later released.
Kest sounds the public warning pattern before binding the crown rope. Petitioners and watch move toward the west lawn; Dorr receives the warning only after it is audible city-wide.

events.note: Kest identifies exact bell operations, while the party’s missing counterkey limits them to binding rather than controlled pin removal or retuning.

events.text: The public warning peal sounds; the crown bell is manually bound at its brake post; witness and mouth bells remain operable; no stage pin is safely removed; Kest, Mela, and Rian become named witnesses.

events.closing_note: The manor warrant has failed, but certified copies, Tavia’s confession, a public-custody pledge, a warning peal, and a physically bound crown bell now exist as separate durable facts.

events.title: The Saint Who Could Not Answer
events.attendance_note: All four independent witnesses present under Iria Vale’s emergency charter.
events.opening_note: The Counterseal Witnesses approach Vale Manor behind a warning crowd while the witness bell remains ready and the crown bell is physically bound.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Iria Vale, Tavia Sorn, Ors Renn, Nessa Quill, Jori Kest, Edrin Vale, Leva Orm, and Peren Holt

events.text: The public approach supplies two independent anchors: certified copies already distributed outside and the warning crowd reading Olyra’s deposition. The group names interim custody before asking Edrin to stand down.
Tavia rejects the involuntary mouth stage in public; Iria acknowledges the Vale concealment; Kest certifies that the crown bell is bound but warns that the witness and mouth notes remain live.
Edrin moves to Witnessed Terms. He permits the witness note as a public demonstration, opens the garden doors, and agrees that no current petition packet will be placed on the vow-bed.

events.note: The witness body cannot recognize the fever doors and repeats a civic slogan instead of Olyra’s deposition; it is unstable evidence, not Olyra restored.

events.text: The witness note forms a translucent figure that recites “open the doors,” “wait for lawful order,” and unrelated pleas. It answers no question and recognizes no personal relic.
A witness-only Glass Saint forms before named observers; it provides no unknown fact, stable personality, or claim to be Olyra.
Edrin steps off the speaker mark and opens the inner mouth knot before the second note; no Vale voice is taken.
The manual crown-bell bind holds through the finale; no crown note launches and neither relay tower receives a command.
Peren lowers and seals the heartglass after the demonstration; the witness body collapses without broken panes or injured servants.
Edrin and Tavia submit to Renn’s named custody. Cooperation is recorded without erasing conspiracy, sabotage, injury, theft, or attempted compulsion.

Interim custody is split: Renn seals the inert heartglass; the House inventories and holds the vow-bed; Senna retains archive originals; certified copies remain distributed; the shrine panes stay shuttered under Leva’s household inventory pending a public hearing.

Olyra’s deposition and the trustee concealment minute receive a witnessed public reading and distributed certified copies, but no infirmary family testimony or physical hospice authentication has yet been obtained.
Dorr’s warrant denial, peal order, and prior concealment minute enter a public inquiry; the adventure does not recast him as an occult conspirator.

The obedience cult fractures publicly around the deposition and witness body; petition caucuses remain divided over relic preservation, prosecution, and whether any future answering rite should be attempted.

events.closing_note: Immediate coercion ends with no stolen voice and no command. The city has a public record, a witnessed but unstable manifestation, divided custody, named accused people, and unresolved arguments about Olyra, the relic, and institutional reform.
